post.description: Public. A hospital, laboratory, radiology unit or pharmacy applies with its name, official email, phone, address and a message. A link goes to the official email; it opens `redirect_url` with `token` and `application` added. The application starts as `submitted`.

post.description: Public, step 2. Send the `application` and `token` from the emailed link, the admin's `email` and their `profile` (names, phone, gender and a staff role the facility type allows). For an observation facility, send this once for each part, with `facility_type` (`laboratory` or `radiology`) and that part's own details in `part` (`name`, `street`, `city`, `state`, `country`, `email` and optional `phone`). A 6-digit code goes to the admin's email, unless it is the official email the link already proved. Send again to get a fresh code (one a minute, five a day). An email a staff account already uses is refused, and so is the other part's admin email.
post.summary: Give a facility application's first admin

post.description: Public. Send the `application`, the `token` from the emailed link and the `code` sent to the admin's email. For an observation facility, also send the part (`facility_type`). A code works once and for 10 minutes.
post.summary: Verify a facility application admin's email

post.description: Public, multipart, the end of step 2. Send the `application`, the `token` from the emailed link, the address (`street`, `city`, `state`, `country`) and one or more `documents` (licence, registration certificate and similar). Refused until the admin's email is verified. The application moves to `in_review` and the link stops working.
post.summary: Submit a facility application's address and documents

post.description: Public. Send the `application` and `token` from the emailed link. The application moves to `email_verified`. Keep the token: the document upload needs it.
post.summary: Verify a facility application's email

post.description: For now only a DH admin may call this. Send the facility's details (`facility_type`, `name`, `official_email`, `phone`), its location (`street`, `city`, `state`, `country`), its first `admins` and the `login_url`. Each admin has an `email` and a `profile` (names, phone, gender and a staff role the facility type allows). An observation facility needs two admins, one with `facility_type` `laboratory` and one `radiology`, each with that part's own details in `part` (`name`, `street`, `city`, `state`, `country`, `email` and optional `phone`). No code is sent: the facility is created active at once, and each admin is emailed a temporary password. An email a staff account already uses is refused.
post.summary: Register a facility in person (field agent)

post.description: A hospital admin adds a laboratory, radiology unit or pharmacy (`facility_type`) with its own `name`, address (`street`, `city`, `state`, `country`) and optional `phone` and `email`, and its first admin (`admin`: email and profile, with a role that unit allows). The unit is attached to the hospital at once. The admin is emailed a temporary password and `login_url`. A hospital has at most one arm of each type.
post.summary: Add an arm to the hospital

post.description: Ends the attachment. The unit becomes a standalone facility and keeps its staff. Refused while the unit has no active admin of its own: name one first.

post.description: Send the sqid of an existing laboratory, radiology unit or pharmacy as `facility`. This only records a pending link: the unit is not attached yet. Refused when the unit is already attached somewhere, the hospital already has an arm of that type, or a link is already pending.

post.description: For a hospital account moved to the new structure. Send the admin's first name, last name, phone, gender and staff role (doctor, nurse or receptionist). Until this is sent the account can use no other endpoint except changing the password.
post.summary: Give a converted hospital account's personal details

post.description: Send `account_type` (`patient` or `staff`), because one email can be both a patient and a staff account. Leave it out only for a DH admin account. Send the same `account_type` to the OTP check.

Send `identifier` (an email, a phone number, or a HIN for patients), the password, and `account_type` (`patient` from the patient app, `staff` from the staff app). Without `account_type`, if the details match both a patient and a staff account, nobody is logged in: the 409 response has code `account_type_required` and lists `account_types`; ask again with one. An unknown identifier and a wrong password give the same 401. The response lists `acting_as`: for staff, their facility and role; for patients, themselves, their dependants and the patients they are a proxy for. `next_step` names what the account must do before anything else, or is null: `admin_details_required` (a converted hospital account sends its details to `/api/auth/first-login`) or `nin_not_verified` (a patient sends their NIN to `/api/auth/nin/verify`). Until then every other endpoint answers 403 with that code, except changing the password.
post.summary: Login a user

post.description: For a logged-in patient whose login response named `nin_not_verified` as the next step. Send only the NIN: the patient comes from the login. The rules are the same as before: three attempts a day, and a NIN another patient already holds is refused. On success it answers like login, and every other endpoint opens up.
post.summary: Verify your own NIN

patch.description: Works for any logged-in user. The old password must be sent too.
patch.summary: Update your account password

post.summary: Resend verification OTP on signup

post.description: Send names, gender, date of birth, `login_url`, and an `email`, a `phone`, or both. A 6-digit code goes to the contact named in `verify_by` (`email` or `phone`); without it, to the email if one was given, otherwise the phone. Only that contact becomes the login. The other one is saved on the patient's profile as contact details. No account is made yet. Sending again with the same contact sends a fresh code (one a minute, five a day) and the old one stops working. The answer is always the same: if the contact already has a patient account, no code is sent and its owner is emailed a way to log in. Text messages are not sent yet.
post.summary: Patient signup, step 1: details

post.description: Send `signup_token`, the 11-digit `nin` and a `password`. The NIN is checked, the account and the patient (with a HIN) are made, and it answers like login. Three NIN attempts a day, counted by the contact and by the NIN. A NIN another patient holds is refused. If something fails after the NIN was accepted, send the same request again: the NIN is not checked twice.
post.summary: Patient signup, step 3: NIN and password

post.description: For a receptionist registering an adult who is with them. The same body and the same answer as patient signup step 1 (`/api/auth/signup`): the code goes to the patient's own email or phone, and the patient reads it out. Step 2 is `/api/auth/signup/verify-code`, as for any signup. No hospital file is made for the patient.
post.summary: Register a patient at the desk, step 1: details

post.description: The same body and checks as patient signup step 3 (`/api/auth/signup/complete`). The patient gives their NIN and chooses a password. The account is made, but nobody is logged in: the answer is the new patient's `hin`, names, gender and date of birth. The patient logs in later on their own device.
post.summary: Register a patient at the desk, step 3: NIN and password

post.description: Sent by a guardian for one of their dependants (`dependant` is the dependant's HIN). Send the dependant's own `email`, `phone` or both, with `verify_by` and `login_url`, as in patient signup step 1. The code goes to that contact. The dependant then sends it to `/api/auth/signup/verify-code` and finishes at `/api/auth/signup/upgrade/complete`. The answer is always the same.
post.summary: Give a dependant their own account, step 1: the contact

post.description: Sent by the dependant with the `signup_token` from `/api/auth/signup/verify-code` and the `password` they choose. The account is attached to the same patient, so the HIN and records stay. The guardian links end. Answers like login, with `next_step` `nin_not_verified`: the NIN is asked for next.
post.summary: Give a dependant their own account, step 3: the password

post.description: Send the same contact as step 1 (with `verify_by` if it was sent) and the code. Returns `signup_token` for step 3. Starting step 1 again makes the token stop working.
post.summary: Patient signup, step 2: the code

post.description: Creates a care task for a patient who is currently admitted to the doctor's hospital. The first scheduled occurrences are created together with the task, so the task appears on the nurse side immediately. The request must include the task type, when it starts, and a 'config' object with details specific to the task type: a procedure name for procedure tasks, the vital signs to monitor for vital signs tasks, an intake/output tracking mode for input/output tasks, a monitoring schedule for glucose tasks, and the fluid details (solution, additives, bag volume, total volume, and rate) for IV fluid tasks. A medication task request carries the drug order inside its config: the order is created and sent to the pharmacy together with the tasks, one task per drug, and the response is a list of tasks. Other task types return a single task object. The 'frequency' and 'duration' values for medication tasks come from each drug's entry, not from the top-level request.
post.summary: Create a task for an admitted patient

get.description: Returns the tasks waiting for a nurse at the authenticated nurse's hospital. Only tasks that are still pending and belong to active admissions are listed; tasks already claimed, finished, missed, escalated, or cancelled by a patient's discharge never appear. Each item includes the patient, what kind of task it is, the doctor's instructions, its priority, when it is scheduled, whether it is upcoming, due, or overdue (a task becomes overdue 30 minutes after its scheduled time), and a short task-specific summary such as the vital signs to record or the drug and dose to give. Results are ordered with overdue and due tasks first, then by priority, then by scheduled time.
get.summary: List the nurse's pending task occurrences

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: Filter by the task's priority.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Number of results to return per page.

parameters.name: timing
parameters.description: Filter by how far the task is from its scheduled time. upcoming: scheduled time has not arrived yet. due: scheduled time has arrived but is less than 30 minutes past. overdue: more than 30 minutes past the scheduled time.

post.description: Claims a pending task for the authenticated nurse and marks it as in progress. If two nurses try to claim the same task at the same time, only the first request succeeds; the other gets an error. Returns the task's new status and who claimed it.
post.summary: Claim a pending task occurrence

post.description: Records that the authenticated nurse has given the medication for a task they previously claimed. Medication tasks have no form to fill in: the drug details were entered by the doctor when the task was created, so confirming only marks the task as finished. Only the nurse who claimed the task can confirm it. A task that is already finished, missed, escalated, cancelled, or never claimed cannot be confirmed.
post.summary: Confirm a claimed medication task occurrence

post.description: Records that the authenticated nurse believes this task needs attention beyond what nursing can do. The request must include a short reason.
post.summary: Escalate a task occurrence

post.description: Completes a task the authenticated nurse has claimed by recording what was actually done. The request body depends on the kind of task: vital signs tasks take the values for the vital signs the doctor selected (submitting a vital sign that is not part of the task is rejected); procedure tasks take consent, the patient's condition after the procedure, estimated blood loss in ml, and the patient's current position; IV fluid tasks take whether to count this administration toward the patient's fluid chart, the IV site condition, the cannula location, and an optional remark; glucose tasks take the reading value and unit, the context such as fasting or pre-meal, and whether insulin was given; input/output tasks take an 'intake' object and/or an 'output' object — whichever sections the task's tracking mode allows. The doctor's details (procedure name, fluid plan) are recorded automatically; the nurse never re-enters them. Medication tasks are confirmed through a separate endpoint instead. Only the nurse who claimed the task can execute it. A task that is finished, missed, escalated, cancelled, or never claimed cannot be executed. If anything fails, nothing is saved and the task stays claimed so it can be retried.
post.summary: Execute a claimed task occurrence

post.description: Records that a task was not performed. Works on a pending task or one the authenticated nurse has claimed; only the nurse who claimed in-progress task can mark it missed. A task that is already finished, missed, escalated, or cancelled cannot be marked missed. Tasks are never marked missed automatically — being overdue does not stop a nurse from completing or acting on them later.
post.summary: Mark a task occurrence as missed

post.description: Gives up ownership of a task the authenticated nurse previously claimed. The task goes back to pending so any nurse at the hospital can claim it again. Only the nurse who claimed the task can release it, and tasks that are finished, missed, escalated, or cancelled can never be released.
post.summary: Release a claimed task occurrence

get.description: Returns every care task created for a patient for the current admission. get.description: Returns the patient's fluid balance for the current day: total intake minus total output, in millilitres, with both totals included so the balance can be explained. The day runs from midnight UTC up to now, so the balance resets at midnight and grows as the day goes on. The calculation is live and never stored: it sums the patient's intake and output records whose observed time falls inside today, including the initial intake and output from the admission note and the intake and output recorded during task execution. The patient comes from the admission, never from the request.
get.summary: Get a patient's fluid balance for today

get.description:
Returns every record made during one hospital stay. It works for current admissions and for discharged ones. The admission must belong to your hospital.

Records are listed oldest first. Each record appears once. If a result was submitted more than once, only the latest one is shown, with its current status. Each entry says what kind of record it is, when it was made and who made it, and holds the record itself in `record`.

Nurses only see SOAP notes that a doctor has shared. Doctors see all of them.

Use `record_type` to see only one kind of record. The kinds on this endpoint are:

- `vital_signs`: Vital signs: blood pressure, temperature, breathing rate, heart rate, height, weight, oxygen level, pain score and notes.
- `drug_record`: A drug the patient was prescribed: name, strength, route, quantity, how often and for how long.
- `lab_test_result`: A lab result: the value of each parameter, comments, interpretation and its status.
- `scan_result`: A scan result: findings, impression, recommendation, who reported it and its status.
- `admission_note`: The nurse's note written when the patient was admitted: allergies, and the mobility, nutrition, fall risk and skin assessments.
- `care_plan`: A nursing care plan: problem, goals, interventions and evaluation.
- `case_note`: A nursing case note: observations, care given, the patient's response, abnormalities and follow-up.
- `progress_note`: A progress note: subjective, objective, assessment and plan.
- `input_record`: Fluid or feed the patient took in: source, route and volume.
- `output_record`: Fluid the patient passed out: type, characteristics, volume and the nurse's remark.
- `procedure_record`: A procedure a nurse carried out: consent, the patient's condition afterwards and estimated blood loss.
- `glucose_record`: A blood sugar reading: value, unit, when it was taken and whether insulin was given.
- `iv_fluid_record`: An IV fluid given: solution, bag volume, infusion rate, site condition and cannula location.
- `seizure_event_log`: A seizure the nurse recorded: how long it lasted, the movements, signs, level of consciousness and what was done.
- `doctor_discharge_form`: The doctor's discharge summary: diagnoses, hospital course, treatment, condition at discharge and follow-up.
- `nurse_discharge_form`: The nurse's discharge checks: devices removed, condition, education given and the final vital signs.
get.summary: List the records made during an admission

post.description: Records a seizure that happened during the admission. The nurse captures what was observed: motor movement, physical signs, the body parts involved, the patient's level of consciousness, how the patient reacted afterward, the duration in minutes and seconds, and any interventions given (free text). Only the duration is required. The 'prolonged or critical' flag on the response is computed by the system, never entered: it is true when the seizure lasted more than five minutes or the patient did not regain consciousness. The patient, hospital, and nurse come from the admission and the logged-in nurse, never from the request. Recording a seizure does not create any task or scheduled work.
post.summary: Record a seizure event for an admitted patient
